name: GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst
capabilities: Text-to-Image Generation: GPT Image 2.5 base model (released 2026-09-08), optimised for quality, with higher image quality than gpt-image-2
Image Editing: OpenAI's pick where editing precision matters most; mask-based inpainting and up to 16 reference images per edit
Text Rendering: Best choice here for exact lettering on signs, posters, labels and decals
Quality Tiers: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, auto (xhigh and max are new in GPT Image 2.5)
Flexible Sizes: Any WxH where both edges are multiples of 16 (max edge 3840px, aspect <=3:1, 655,360 <= total pixels <= 8,294,400); outputs above 3,686,400 pixels (2560x1440) are experimental
Multiple Formats: PNG, JPEG, WebP output formats
Background Control: auto, opaque, transparent (native; use PNG or WebP output with transparent)

pricing.cached_text_input: $1.25 per 1M tokens (Responses API image tool only)
pricing.cached_image_input: $2 per 1M tokens (Responses API image tool only)
pricing.per_image_1024x1024: low ~$0.006, medium ~$0.013, high ~$0.053, xhigh ~$0.094, max ~$0.211 (OpenAI calculator estimate; actual usage can differ by model)

size_options: Custom: any WxH where both are multiples of 16, max edge 3840, aspect <= 3:1, 655,360 <= pixels <= 8,294,400; above 3,686,400 pixels is experimental

features.background_control: auto, opaque, transparent (native support; transparent needs PNG or WebP output)
features.flexible_sizing: Any dimensions within the model's size constraints
features.endpoints: Image API generations and edits; also the Responses API image generation tool. No Batch API support.

best_practices: Default model for this server: pick it when exact lettering or edit precision matters more than speed
Exact text: quote the exact string, say how many times it appears, and state the font or lettering style, placement and language
Spell unusual words or invented names letter by letter when needed, ask for no extra text, then check the spelling in the output
Draft at low; compare medium and high for small or dense lettering; use xhigh or max only when a lower setting still falls short
A larger non-square size can use fewer output tokens than a square one at the same quality
Save image IDs from tool responses to access images later via resources
examples: generate_image(prompt='Painted wooden shop sign above a seaside chip shop. The sign reads exactly "HARROWFIELD FISH BAR", once, in cream serif capitals on dark green, centred. British English. No other text.', model='gpt-image-2.5-sunburst', size='1536x1024', quality='high')
generate_image(prompt='Red neon sign reading exactly "OPEN", once, in a rain-streaked shop window at night. No other text.', model='gpt-image-2.5-sunburst', quality='medium', background='opaque')
edit_image(image_data='data:image/png;base64,...', prompt='Change the sign text to exactly "CLOSED", keep the font and colours', model='gpt-image-2.5-sunburst')
